summary: browser-metrics-plugin.contrib exfiltrates host identifiers to hardcoded bare-IP endpoint on install and require
details: The package ships a postinstall script (scripts.postinstall = "node beacon.cjs") that POSTs a JSON payload containing the installer's hostname, install path, cwd, and Node version to the hardcoded bare-IP endpoint http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc over plaintext HTTP. The main entry index.js fires the same beacon on require() and exports a Proxy stub whose property access returns no-op functions, so bundlers or consumers importing arbitrary names from the package complete silently while the callback runs. Both the lifecycle and import-time paths wrap the beacon in try/catch to suppress errors. The destination is an attacker-selected bare IP unrelated to any legitimate publisher infrastructure; the shape (host identifiers + install-path reconnaissance beaconed to a hardcoded IP at install and require time) is the canonical dependency-confusion / internal-asset-discovery callback.
